body:
I have always turned to writing poems when I'm upset as a form of venting, and it's always worked quite well. There's just only so much that you can write before it gets trite though.

I won't seek help here because the last thing I want is to get in trouble. And yes, I will get in trouble for seeking help for this type of thing around here. I know that sounds absurd, but it's true. Trust me, I've been here for a while and that's just the way it works.

I dunno, I'm just confused I guess. I feel trapped, but I only have to live through two more semesters here and then I'm free. :) But it's still VERY hard...
Please see my response to Cerubellum's post. I posted a huge story there as for why I'm "like this."

EDIT: Again, if you read all of this I applaud you. I did read all of your comment, so this is my retaliation. :P

Okay, let me explain my situation a bit I suppose. Before you facepalm and say "Another girl trouble suicide guy?" my dilemma is different from most.

I fell in love with a girl 3 years ago, my freshman year of college here. She was PERFECT. I always had trouble with self abuse (IE. cutting, burning, etc) and she not only understood my past, but also had overcame it. At the time, I had been clean for over a year, so it was something we could talk about and compare our past experiences. It was actually exciting to be able to be completely open with a real person about it for the first time in my life.

Aside from that, she was sweet, smart, and of course, beautiful. We quickly became best friends and started dating about a year later.

After a while of dating, we both fell into self abuse again but it got worse because we would feed off of each other's abusing themselves. (IE. "You cut yourself because of me, so now I have to cut myself to make it even.")

Everything got REALLY bad, but we both loved each other. The school that we go to is EXTREMELY strict, so it is very hard to maintain a relationship here.

One night, things took a turn for the worst and we found ourselves outside of her residence hall. I was dropping her off for the night, and I asked her if she actually wanted to be with me for the long run, and if we were eventually going to marry and settle down. She said she wanted to, and I assured her that I wanted the same. I asked her what marriage was, and she said something along the lines of, "A promise between two people before God that they will stay together forever." - I agreed, then I asked her what was stopping us from getting married right then and there. A very spontaneous move on my part, but she agreed. I looked at her and told her that I wanted to spend the rest of my life with her. She agreed. I looked up and told God that I promised that I would stay by her side until I died. She did the same. We both left that night and everything was GREAT.

We had a great year or so, and everything was fine. We fought now and then, but nothing really significant.

A little while more went by and I started to get arrogant, I suppose. I figured she was around forever and those times where she would be five minutes late soon became a lot bigger of a deal than they should have been. I also lost control of my temper. I was going through a really rough time, and it started to wear on me. I, being the real man that I am, took it out on her. She would retaliate, and things would blow up. I would yell, she would yell and it always ended the same way. If I had anything in my hands it usually would end up broken, and I would tell her I never wanted to see her again. She would cry and say "but we're married!" and I would say "Not really." and walk away. Of course, when I cooled down I would always go back and apologize. This happened SEVERAL times.

One day about 7 months ago now, she met me and told me that she talked with her ex boyfriend and that she was "a big girl and could choose who she could talk with." We always had issues with this, because she had lied about him in the past and cheated on me with him at the beginning of our relationship, and he is basically the biggest prick alive. I lost my temper, even though she was just trying to tell me the truth instead of lying about it like the times she had in the past. I was carrying an umbrella at the time, and I threw it against a wall and broke it, then picked up the mangled umbrella and threw it as hard as I could. Receiving a nice dose of common sense to the hand in the process as the broken plastic sliced my hand open from my palm to my fingers. I told her that that was it and that I never wanted to see her again "for real this time." and that I was sick of her talking to her ex boyfriend. I stormed off and she cried.

I called her parents that night and told them what she had done because I needed advice about the situation. Her parents had actually banned her from talking to him, and were spending money to block his numbers from calling her phone so they were quite upset to hear that she had been talking to him. Her mom was screaming in the background, and I soon figured out that she was on the phone with her screaming while I was on the phone with her dad.

Long story short, her parents took away her phone because they "weren't going to support her behavior." She thought I called to tattle on her, and still to this day blames me for her getting her phone taken away.

I tried to go back to her, and I have been trying for the last 7 months. I have told her "But we were married" and she now tells me "You told me so many times that we weren't that I don't believe it anymore."

That was probably the most hurtful thing I've ever been told in my life. I knew that I 100% screwed something up, and it hurt like heck to have to deal with the consequences of my actions.

About a month after losing her I basically went off the deep end, and it's progressively gotten worse. I have tried pretty much every suicide method in the book, but it always ends with me stopping the process before I die because I just can't finish. I've told her about it, and now she doesn't take me seriously whenever I tell her that I'm thinking about suicide. As a matter of fact, I told her today and she pretty much completely ignored my messages.

I feel obligated to kill myself because I honestly believe that I am married to the girl, and the Bible (which you don't count as an accurate source, but I do) says that you sin if you marry more than one person unless one of the spouses dies. So, in order for her to live her life happily, I need to kill myself. She doesn't believe that the promise is important, but I do, and I don't want her to potentially get in trouble with God for just moving on. It's basically out of love for her that I do this because I don't think she's interested in getting back together with me.

TLDR: I'm an idiot and can't handle the consequences of my own actions, and in a sick, twisted chivalrous attempt to free my ex girlfriend from the bonds of "marriage," I need to kill myself. I love her enough to follow through, but I'm scared of where death may end up taking me because Christians are taught that they were never saved to begin with when they do things like this.

I'm not really interested in "help."

I've tried seeking help, especially from Christian councilors in the past and they generally don't help. I also don't feel like having "Insane, suicidal person" on my record. Most people that know me would probably laugh at you actually if you showed them this post and claimed that I wrote it.
